title: Degree-one line quotients give maps to relative Proj over an algebraic space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $X,Y$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}\mathcal A_n$ be a commutative unital graded $\mathcal O_X$-algebra on the small etale site [def-trf-etale-graded-module-algebra], with $\mathcal A_0=\mathcal O_X$ and each degree quasi-coherent [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume that $\mathcal A$ is generated in degree one, meaning that the multiplication maps $\mathcal A_1^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal A_n$ are surjective for all $n\geq1$. Let $p:P_X(\mathcal A)\to X$ be the relative Proj of [lem-sfb-space-relative-proj-scheme-tests]. Given an $S$-morphism $f:Y\to X$, a line module $L$ on $Y$ (a module locally isomorphic to $\mathcal O_Y$), and a graded unital algebra map $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L^{\otimes n}$ whose degree-one map is surjective as a map of sheaves, there is a canonical $S$-morphism $r_{f,L,\psi}:Y\to P_X(\mathcal A)$ satisfying $p\circ r_{f,L,\psi}=f$. Pullback and tensor are those of [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The canonical map is normalized as follows: after any scheme charts on $X$ and $Y$, on a locus trivializing $L$ where the image of a degree-one homogeneous section $a$ generates $L$, it lands in $D_+(a)$ and the map on degree-zero homogeneous fractions sends $v/a^n$ to $\psi_n(v)/\psi_1(a)^n$. Here the quotient is taken in the chosen trivialization of $L$; changing that trivialization cancels the same unit to the power $n$ in numerator and denominator. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, Noetherian, or finite generation assumption is made.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1), applied to the line-quotient datum; its scheme-test representation gives the algebraic-space-source formulation by etale descent. Chart normalization is Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj).

proof.text: Choose a representable surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to X$. The fibre product $Y_V=Y\times_XV$ is an algebraic space, and $Y_V\to Y$ is surjective etale. Choose a scheme atlas $T\to Y_V$ and put $t:T\to Y$ for the composite. It is a representable surjective etale scheme presentation: for an $S$-scheme $W$ and $h_W\to Y$, the test $W\times_YY_V=W\times_XV$ is a scheme, surjective etale over $W$, and $W\times_YT=(W\times_XV)\times_{Y_V}T$ is a scheme, surjective etale over it; a composite of surjective etale scheme morphisms is surjective etale. Write $g:T\to V$. Both $R=T\times_YT$ and $V_2=V\times_XV$ are schemes, by representability of the diagonals. The two maps $R\rightrightarrows T\to V$ give $R\to V_2$. These are scheme overlaps, not assumed affine. Let $P=P_X(\mathcal A)$; its scheme-test comparison identifies $V\times_XP$ with $\operatorname{Proj}_V((\mathcal A|_V)_{\mathrm{Zar}})$.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: Restrict the given data to these etale charts. Put $\mathcal A_V=(\mathcal A|_V)_{\mathrm{Zar}}$ and $L_T=(L|_T)_{\mathrm{Zar}}$. The scheme Zariski--etale equivalence identifies $L_T$ with an ordinary invertible module and identifies $g^*\mathcal A_V$ with the Zariski form of $t^*f^*\mathcal A$. Use the specified composition comparison and the tensor comparison to transport $\psi|_T$ to a graded map $\psi_T:g^*\mathcal A_V\to\bigoplus_{n\geq0}L_T^{\otimes n}$. Multiplication and units are transported degreewise. The degree-one map remains surjective: etale restriction is localization of the site, and the additive equivalence preserves cokernels and hence epimorphisms. The same construction applies to $R\to V_2$ and to refinements of these charts. No flatness of $f$ is used.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: On an affine base open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A_0\subset V$ and an affine $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\subset g^{-1}U$ trivializing $L_T$, write $\psi_T(a)=b_a e$ for $a\in\mathcal A_{V,1}(U)$. The affine pullback formula identifies the degree-one source on $W$ with $\mathcal A_{V,1}(U)\otimes_{A_0}B$. At any $w\in W$, surjectivity onto $B_w e$ expresses $e$ as a finite $B_w$-linear combination of these images. Thus the $b_a$ generate the unit ideal in $B_w$. Since $B_w$ is local, some $b_a$ is a unit there. Hence the opens $D(b_a)$, with $a$ in degree one, cover $W$. Varying $U,W$ proves that the degree-one generator loci cover all of $T$. This is a local argument, so it requires no finite cover or finite generation of the algebra.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: Apply the existing scheme fraction-chart atlas to $(g,\mathcal A_V,L_T,\psi_T)$. On each generator locus $T_a$ it supplies a map to $D_+(a)$ with $v/a^n\mapsto\psi_{T,n}(v)/\psi_{T,1}(a)^n$. Its statement gives agreement of these maps inside relative Proj on every pairwise intersection, including different affine base opens. Step 3 shows that the degree-one loci already cover $T$. Scheme-morphism gluing therefore gives a unique $q:T\to\operatorname{Proj}_V(\mathcal A_V)$ with these formulas. The chart maps are over their base affine opens (the degree-zero structural scalar maps to its pullback), so $q$ is over $V$. The same construction gives $q_2:R\to\operatorname{Proj}_{V_2}(\mathcal A|_{V_2})$. Compose $q$ with $V\times_XP\to P$ to obtain $\widetilde q:T\to P$.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: For each projection $s_i:R\to T$, consider the commutative scheme square with lower map $\operatorname{pr}_i:V_2\to V$ and upper map $s_i$. The data on $R\to V_2$ are the pullbacks of those on $T\to V$: both are restrictions of the original data, with the tensor-normalized composition comparisons of step 2. The scheme chart-pullback statement applies to $q_2$ and $q$ and gives $c_i\circ q_2=q\circ s_i$, where $c_i$ is the relative-Proj comparison for $V_2\to V$. Its hypotheses require only the displayed commutative square and the fraction formulas established in step 4, not a cartesian square or a flat morphism. Scheme-test compatibility for $P$ identifies both compositions $\operatorname{Proj}_{V_2}(\mathcal A|_{V_2})\to P$ with the same projection to $P$. Consequently $\widetilde q\circ s_1=\widetilde q\circ s_2$. This proves the actual descent equation.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: Apply etale chart-morphism descent to the presentation $t:T\to Y$, target $P$, and invariant open $O=T$. The equality in step 5 is precisely its required relation. Since the open is the whole atlas, the descended open subspace is all of $Y$. We obtain a unique $S$-morphism $r:Y\to P$ with $r\circ t=\widetilde q$. After precomposition with $t$, both $p\circ r$ and $f$ equal $f\circ t$, because $q$ is over $V$. The equality-detection clause of the same descent statement, with target $X$, implies $p\circ r=f$.

source.place: Tag 085D (lemma-relative-proj-generated-in-degree-1), part (1): scheme construction and etale descent; Tag 0D2Z (lemma-invertible-map-into-relative-proj), scheme-chart characterization (3).

proof.text: The construction is independent of the atlases: two choices have a common etale scheme refinement obtained by fibre products and a scheme atlas; applying step 5 to its scheme comparison squares identifies the two maps there. Descent detects their equality on $Y$. The same comparison with any further scheme charts shows that $r$ has the required fraction normalization on them. Uniqueness follows by covering each such chart by its degree-one generator loci and using scheme gluing, then etale descent. Finally, replacing a frame $e$ by $ue$ replaces the coefficient of $\psi_n(v)$ by $u^{-n}$ times that coefficient and that of $\psi_1(a)$ by $u^{-1}$ times its coefficient; their ratio is unchanged. Thus the canonical map has exactly the specified normalization. Empty charts contribute the unique empty-domain map; the argument nowhere requires a nonempty space.

lean.statement: theorem existsUnique_spaceProj_degreeOne_quotient (C : SpaceProjCoefficients S) {X Y : AlgebraicSpace S} (A : SpaceProjInput X) (R : SpaceProjRealization C A) (_hzero : IsIso A.algebra.unit) (_hgen : ∀ (W : Over S) (g : schemeSpace W ⟶ X) (V : W.left.affineOpens), Algebra.adjoin Γ(W.left, V.1) (Set.range (fun a : (C.scheme A W g).affine.grading V 1 ↦ a.val)) = ⊤) (f : Y ⟶ X) (L : Y.Modules) (hL : Y.IsLineModule L) (ψ : SpaceProjLineQuotient C A f (lineTestFamily Y L hL)) (_hψ : ψ.IsSurjectiveInDegreeOne) : ∃! r : Y ⟶ R.space, ψ.IsCanonicalMap R r
lean.note: The homogeneous algebra map is written in its adjoint cartesian scheme-test presentation, using the existing lineTestFamily of the given small-etale line module and the normalized C.scheme coefficients. Its products, units and arbitrary scheme-base-change equations are fields, not additional input hypotheses. Degree-one surjectivity is the equivalent local lifted-basis condition. IsCanonicalMap specifies actual D_+(a) factorizations and intrinsic cross-multiplied homogeneous-fraction equations on every scheme test and source open. The coefficient and Proj realization are those of the recorded relative-Proj dependency; no additional geometric assumption is imposed.
